standard_prerequisites.name: Homotopies and quasi-inverse data
standard_prerequisites.statement: f : A -> B and g : B -> A with homotopies eta : g o f ~ id and epsilon : f o g ~ id.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the data of the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Naturality of a homotopy
standard_prerequisites.statement: A homotopy between composites satisfies the standard naturality square on paths.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is used at source lines 189 and 201 to build the diagrams.

standard_prerequisites.name: Commutation of eta with g o f
standard_prerequisites.statement: The homotopy eta : g o f ~ id commutes with g o f in the sense of the displayed identity.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the labelled input used at source line 197.

core_obligations: Observe that it suffices to prove one direction, since the other follows by replacing A, f, eta with B, g, epsilon (source line 186).
Start from tau : prd x:A, f(eta x) = epsilon(f x), fix y : B, and use naturality of epsilon together with the action of g to build the first commuting diagram of paths (source lines 187-192).
Apply tau at g y to the left-hand side of the diagram, producing the second diagram (source lines 193-196).
Use the retained commutation of eta with g o f to rewrite the left vertical arrow (source lines 197-200).
Compare with the diagram obtained from naturality of eta, cancel the outer homotopies and read off g(epsilon y) = eta(g y) (source lines 201-205).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce to one direction and build the first commuting diagram.
Insert tau(gy) and use the retained commutation relation.
Compare with naturality of eta and cancel.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `lem:coh-equiv` at source lines 178-184: for f, g and homotopies eta, epsilon, the condition prd x, f(eta x) = epsilon(f x) is logically equivalent to prd y, g(epsilon y) = eta(g y). The author's proof (source lines 185-206) is a diagram chase in the type theory: it reduces to one direction by symmetry (line 186), builds a first commuting square from naturality of epsilon composed with g (lines 189-192), inserts tau(gy) on the left-hand side to obtain a second square (lines 193-196), replaces the left vertical arrow using the retained commutation relation (lines 197-200), compares with the square coming from naturality of eta (lines 201-204) and cancels everything except the right-hand homotopy (line 205). The statement is a bare equivalence of two product types and records neither the diagrams nor which naturality is used where.
